model_size_sweep_2026_07_26.config: int4_awq backbone, lm_head left fp16 -- deliberately mirrors the shipped 8B so model size is the only variable
model_size_sweep_2026_07_26.verdict: SIGNIFICANT loss: -11.0 pts vs FP16 8B and -8.6 pts vs INT4 8B, p=0.005. Contrast with quantization on 8B, where every comparison was NOT significant (p>0.4). => quantize aggressively, keep the big model.
model_size_sweep_2026_07_26.note_bandwidth: 1.364 GB / 13.41 ms = 101.7 GB/s = only 67% of the 152.3 GB/s achievable ceiling, vs 97% for the 8B INT4. Smaller models achieve LOWER bandwidth efficiency, so the byte-ratio prediction (9.3 ms) over-predicted the speedup; same direction as the INT4-vs-FP16 efficiency drop measured in K1.

lm_head_quantization_attempt_2026_07_26.status: BLOCKED on T4 memory -- not achieved, prediction remains unverified
lm_head_quantization_attempt_2026_07_26.why_blocked: Two-sided squeeze on 2x T4 (14.56 GiB each): caps high enough to keep every module on GPU leave <1.16 GiB free on the card holding lm_head -> CUDA OOM in modelopt's fake_quantize; caps low enough to free that room spill modules to CPU -> AWQ calibration dies with 'illegal memory access' under accelerate's offload hook. max_memory bounds only initial placement, so quantization state refills to the same water line regardless (v3 and v5 OOMed with identical 1006.81 MiB free).
lm_head_quantization_attempt_2026_07_26.path_forward: Needs a single GPU >=24 GB (L4/A6000/A100) so the 8B + a 1.16 GiB temp fit without sharding, avoiding both failure modes. cloud/colab_export_quant.ipynb already targets Colab, which offers L4/A100 but requires an interactive session.
